title: Acts Chapter 14 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 14 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 14 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 14.

questions.question: In Acts 14, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: They fled unto Lystra and Derbe
They went into the synagogue of the Jews
A man impotent in his feet was healed
The multitude of the city was divided
questions.correctAnswer: They went into the synagogue of the Jews
questions.explanation: Acts 14:1 describes them going into the synagogue of the Jews first before any other event listed.

questions.question: Where did Paul and Barnabas speak so that a great multitude believed?
options: In the synagogue of the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: In the synagogue of the Jews
questions.explanation: Acts 14:1 states they went both together into the synagogue of the Jews and spoke there.

questions.question: Who stirred up the Gentiles against the brethren?
questions.explanation: Acts 14:2 states the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles and made their minds evil affected against the brethren.

questions.question: What did the Lord give testimony unto through Paul and Barnabas?
questions.explanation: Acts 14:3 says the Lord gave testimony unto the word of his grace through them.

questions.question: What was done by the hands of Paul and Barnabas as a sign?
questions.explanation: Acts 14:3 states that the Lord granted signs and wonders to be done by their hands.

questions.question: How did the multitude of the city respond to Paul and Barnabas?
questions.explanation: Acts 14:4 states the multitude of the city was divided; part held with the Jews, and part with the apostles.

questions.question: Who made an assault to stone Paul and Barnabas?
options: Both the Gentiles and Jews with their rulers
questions.correctAnswer: Both the Gentiles and Jews with their rulers
questions.explanation: Acts 14:5 says an assault was made by both the Gentiles and the Jews with their rulers to stone them.

questions.question: Where did Paul and Barnabas flee after being aware of the assault?
questions.explanation: Acts 14:6 states they fled unto Lystra and Derbe, cities of Lycaonia.

questions.question: What did Paul and Barnabas do in Lystra and Derbe?
questions.explanation: Acts 14:7 clearly says there they preached the gospel.

questions.question: What condition did the man sitting at Lystra have?
options: He was impotent in his feet
questions.correctAnswer: He was impotent in his feet
questions.explanation: Acts 14:8 states the man was impotent in his feet, a cripple from his mother's womb.

questions.question: What did Paul perceive about the man in Lystra?
options: That he had faith to be healed
That he was a believer already
questions.correctAnswer: That he had faith to be healed
questions.explanation: Acts 14:9 says Paul perceived that the man had faith to be healed.

questions.question: True or False: Paul and Barnabas spoke boldly in the Lord for a long time.
questions.explanation: Acts 14:3 states they abode speaking boldly in the Lord for a long time.

questions.question: True or False: The man in Lystra who was healed had never walked since his birth.
questions.explanation: Acts 14:8 states he was a cripple from his mother's womb who never had walked.

questions.question: True or False: The text says Paul and Barnabas wrote letters to the churches in Iconium.
questions.explanation: The text does not mention Paul and Barnabas writing letters to the churches in Iconium in these verses.

questions.question: True or False: The text says that the apostles built a synagogue in Lystra.
questions.explanation: There is no mention in these verses of the apostles building a synagogue in Lystra.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 14 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 14 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the people say when they saw what Paul had done?
options: The gods are come down to us in the likeness of men.
We must sacrifice to the living God.
questions.correctAnswer: The gods are come down to us in the likeness of men.
questions.explanation: This is found in Acts 14:11, where the people lifted up their voices in Lycaonia after witnessing a miracle performed by Paul.

questions.question: What does Acts 14:15 promise will happen if someone turns from vanities to the living God?
options: They will be filled with gladness.
questions.correctAnswer: They will be filled with gladness.
questions.explanation: Acts 14:15 mentions turning to the living God, which leads to a life filled with good things, including gladness as stated in Acts 14:17.

questions.question: Who did the people call Barnabas?
questions.explanation: According to Acts 14:12, the people called Barnabas Jupiter due to his stature and role as the chief speaker.

questions.question: What did Paul and Barnabas do when they heard the people were going to sacrifice to them?
options: They ran among the people, crying out.
questions.correctAnswer: They ran among the people, crying out.
questions.explanation: Acts 14:14 states that upon hearing of the people's intentions to sacrifice, they tore their clothes and ran to stop them.

questions.question: What is suggested about God's dealings with nations in Acts 14:16?
options: He suffered all nations to walk in their own ways.
He has chosen a specific nation.
questions.correctAnswer: He suffered all nations to walk in their own ways.
questions.explanation: Acts 14:16 indicates that God allowed nations to follow their own paths before revealing Himself through His messengers.

questions.question: How did God show His goodness to the people, according to Acts 14:17?
options: By giving them rain from heaven and fruitful seasons.
questions.correctAnswer: By giving them rain from heaven and fruitful seasons.
questions.explanation: Acts 14:17 highlights God's provision through nature as evidence of His goodness to all people.

questions.question: What did the people do after Paul healed the crippled man?
questions.explanation: Acts 14:11 shows that the people lifted their voices and initially regarded Paul and Barnabas as gods due to the miracle.

questions.question: What was the reaction of Paul and Barnabas to being called gods?
options: They tore their clothes and protested.
questions.correctAnswer: They tore their clothes and protested.
questions.explanation: In Acts 14:14, Paul and Barnabas expressed their distress by tearing their clothes and running to stop the sacrifices.

questions.question: What happened to Paul after he was stoned by certain Jews?
options: He rose up and entered the city.
questions.correctAnswer: He rose up and entered the city.
questions.explanation: Acts 14:20 narrates that after being stoned, Paul miraculously rose up and returned to the city.

questions.question: What did Paul preach to the people according to Acts 14:15?
options: To worship the gods of the land.
To turn from vanities unto the living God.
questions.correctAnswer: To turn from vanities unto the living God.
questions.explanation: Acts 14:15 records Paul's message urging the people to turn away from their empty practices and seek the true God.

questions.question: What did Paul perceive in the crippled man before healing him?
options: He had faith to be healed.
questions.correctAnswer: He had faith to be healed.
questions.explanation: In Acts 14:9, Paul recognized the man's faith as a prerequisite for his healing.

questions.question: What was the nature of the division in the city as described in Acts 14:4?
options: It was between the rich and the poor.
It was between the Jews and the apostles.
It was between the Romans and the locals.
questions.correctAnswer: It was between the Jews and the apostles.
questions.explanation: Acts 14:4 indicates that the city was divided with some siding with the Jews and others with Paul and Barnabas.

questions.question: Is it true that Paul and Barnabas were mistaken for gods by the people?
questions.explanation: Acts 14:11 states that the people believed Paul and Barnabas were gods due to the miracle performed by Paul.

questions.question: Is it false that Paul was killed by the stoning from the Jews?
questions.explanation: Acts 14:19-20 explains that although Paul was stoned and presumed dead, he actually rose up and re-entered the city.

questions.question: Is it false that Barnabas was called Mercurius by the people?
questions.explanation: Acts 14:12 specifies that the people called Barnabas Jupiter, not Mercurius, indicating a mix-up in their identities.

hard.title: Acts Chapter 14 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 14.

questions.question: What did Paul and Barnabas do after preaching the gospel to a city?
options: They returned again to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch
They wrote letters to the churches
questions.correctAnswer: They returned again to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch
questions.explanation: This is stated in Acts 14:21, where it describes their return to these cities after preaching the gospel.

questions.question: What did Paul and Barnabas exhort the disciples to do?
questions.explanation: Acts 14:22 mentions that Paul and Barnabas confirmed and exhorted the souls of the disciples to continue in the faith.

questions.question: What action did Paul and Barnabas take regarding elders in the churches?
options: They did not involve themselves with leadership
questions.explanation: Acts 14:23 states that Paul and Barnabas ordained elders in every church.

questions.question: To which region did Paul and Barnabas travel after passing through Pisidia?
questions.explanation: Acts 14:24 indicates that after passing through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.

questions.question: Where did Paul and Barnabas go after preaching in Perga?
questions.explanation: Acts 14:25 mentions that after preaching the word in Perga, they went down into Attalia.

questions.question: What did Paul and Barnabas do when they returned to Antioch?
options: Rehearsed all that God had done
questions.correctAnswer: Rehearsed all that God had done
questions.explanation: Acts 14:27 states that upon gathering the church together in Antioch, they rehearsed all that God had done with them.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'kerysso' (κερύνσσω) in Acts 14:25 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Kerysso' means 'to proclaim' as it relates to preaching the word, which is the context of Acts 14:25.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in Acts 14:15, where Paul and Barnabas say they are men of like passions?
questions.explanation: The verse uses parallelism to juxtapose the humanity of Paul and Barnabas with their divine message.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of confirming believers as seen in Acts 14:22?
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 3:2 also discusses sending someone to strengthen and encourage the faith of believers, paralleling the action in Acts 14:22.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage reflects the theme of entering the kingdom through tribulation as noted in Acts 14:22?
questions.explanation: 2 Timothy 3:12 states that all who desire to live godly will suffer persecution, echoing the theme in Acts 14:22 about tribulation.

questions.question: What comes before Acts 14:21?
questions.explanation: Acts 14:20 describes how Paul rose up after being stoned, which directly precedes the events of Acts 14:21.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'pisteuo' (πιστεύω) in Acts 14:23 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Pisteuo' means 'to believe,' which is the context of Acts 14:23 as it refers to those who believed in the Lord.

questions.question: Which literary device is illustrated by the actions of Paul and Barnabas in Acts 14:27 when they recount their experiences?
questions.explanation: Acts 14:27 employs narrative as Paul and Barnabas recount their missionary experiences to the church.

questions.question: True or False: Paul and Barnabas faced no challenges during their missionary journey as described in Acts 14.
questions.explanation: Acts 14:22 states that they must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God, indicating they faced significant challenges.

questions.question: True or False: The apostles were mistaken for gods by the people in Lystra according to Acts 14:11.
questions.explanation: Acts 14:11 recounts how the people of Lystra lifted up their voices, believing Paul and Barnabas were gods due to the miracle performed.

theological.title: Acts Chapter 14 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 14 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 14:3 teach about the means by which God confirms the gospel message?
options: God confirms the gospel through signs and wonders performed by the apostles
God confirms the gospel solely through the written Scriptures
God confirms the gospel by immediate angelic revelation
God confirms the gospel by human wisdom and persuasion
questions.correctAnswer: God confirms the gospel through signs and wonders performed by the apostles
questions.explanation: Acts 14:3 states that God gave testimony to the word of His grace by granting signs and wonders to be done by their hands, showing that God confirms the gospel through miraculous works accompanying preaching.

questions.question: What doctrine about human religious response is taught in Acts 14:15?
options: Humans are prone to idolatry and must be called to repentance toward the living God
Humans naturally worship the true God without error
Humans should maintain their cultural religious traditions without change
Humans are incapable of recognizing any divine being
questions.correctAnswer: Humans are prone to idolatry and must be called to repentance toward the living God
questions.explanation: In Acts 14:15, Paul and Barnabas rebuke the people for worshiping them as gods and call them to turn from these vanities to the living God, teaching the doctrine of human sinfulness and idolatry.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning perseverance and suffering is taught in Acts 14:22?
options: Believers must endure much tribulation to enter the kingdom of God
Salvation is guaranteed without any suffering
Faith is preserved only through human effort
Tribulation is a sign of God’s rejection
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must endure much tribulation to enter the kingdom of God
questions.explanation: Acts 14:22 exhorts believers to continue in the faith and teaches that through much tribulation we must enter the kingdom of God, emphasizing the doctrine of perseverance through suffering.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 14:17 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Acts 14:17 highlights that God gave rain from heaven and fruitful seasons, showing His providential care for creation and humanity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly evident in Acts 14:20 regarding Paul's recovery after being stoned?
questions.explanation: Acts 14:20 shows that although Paul was stoned and left for dead, he rose again, demonstrating God’s sovereign power over life and death.

questions.question: How does Acts 14:1–7 connect to the broader biblical theme of the inclusion of Gentiles into God's covenant people?
options: It shows the gospel beginning to be preached effectively to both Jews and Greeks, preparing for Gentile inclusion
It emphasizes strict Jewish exclusivism without outreach to Gentiles
It focuses solely on Jewish synagogue worship
It portrays Gentiles as permanently excluded from salvation
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the gospel beginning to be preached effectively to both Jews and Greeks, preparing for Gentile inclusion
questions.explanation: Acts 14:1–7 records both Jews and Greeks believing the gospel, indicating the expansion of God’s covenant promises beyond Israel, a major redemptive-historical theme.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme is prepared for by the events described in Acts 14:26–27?
options: The establishment of the church as a mission base for Gentile evangelism
The restoration of the Davidic monarchy
The return of the Jewish exile
questions.correctAnswer: The establishment of the church as a mission base for Gentile evangelism
questions.explanation: Acts 14:26–27 describes the apostles reporting how God opened the door of faith to the Gentiles, preparing for the church’s mission to the nations.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Acts 14:15 and 14:17 teach about God's relationship to human idolatry and revelation?
options: God reveals Himself providentially to all nations, even as humans turn to idolatry
God ignores human idolatry and does not reveal Himself
God punishes all nations immediately for idolatry without any witness
God only reveals Himself to the Jewish people
questions.correctAnswer: God reveals Himself providentially to all nations, even as humans turn to idolatry
questions.explanation: Verse 14:15 calls people to turn from idolatry, while 14:17 explains that God did not leave Himself without witness by giving rain and fruitful seasons, showing His providential revelation despite human sin.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 14:22 and 14:23 teach about the role of church leadership and perseverance?
options: The church ordains elders to strengthen believers to endure tribulation and continue in faith
Church leadership is unnecessary for perseverance
Perseverance is purely an individual responsibility with no communal support
Elders are ordained primarily for political governance
questions.correctAnswer: The church ordains elders to strengthen believers to endure tribulation and continue in faith
questions.explanation: Acts 14:22 exhorts perseverance through tribulation, and 14:23 shows elders ordained and prayed for to support believers, teaching the importance of leadership in sanctification.

questions.question: What combined theological insight about human faith and divine healing is taught in Acts 14:9–10 and 14:19–20?
options: Faith in God’s power is necessary for healing, but believers may still suffer persecution without guaranteed protection
Faith automatically prevents any suffering or harm
Divine healing is unrelated to faith and always occurs
Persecution means lack of faith and no healing
questions.correctAnswer: Faith in God’s power is necessary for healing, but believers may still suffer persecution without guaranteed protection
questions.explanation: Acts 14:9–10 shows Paul perceiving faith for healing, but 14:19–20 shows Paul suffering stoning and nearly dying, illustrating that faith does not exempt from suffering.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that the stoning of Paul in Acts 14:19-20 shows the failure of God’s protection over apostles. What does Acts 14:19-20 actually teach?
options: God sovereignly permits suffering but preserves life to continue the mission
God fails to protect His servants from harm
Apostles have no divine protection and are abandoned
Suffering proves apostles lack true authority
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly permits suffering but preserves life to continue the mission
questions.explanation: Acts 14:19-20 shows Paul was stoned and left for dead, yet God preserved his life so he could continue preaching, indicating divine sovereignty over suffering and mission.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of human passions is taught in Acts 14:15?
options: Apostles share the same passions as their hearers, affirming their genuine humanity
Apostles are divine beings without human passions
Human passions make apostles incapable of ministry
Human passions are sinful and should be rejected entirely
questions.correctAnswer: Apostles share the same passions as their hearers, affirming their genuine humanity
questions.explanation: Acts 14:15 states that Paul and Barnabas are men of like passions, emphasizing the true humanity of apostles.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is reflected in Acts 14:16 concerning God’s patience with nations?
questions.explanation: Acts 14:16 says God suffered all nations to walk in their own ways, demonstrating His longsuffering patience with human sinfulness.

questions.question: How does Acts 14:23 contribute to the doctrine of church order and spiritual discipline?
options: The church ordains elders with prayer and fasting, emphasizing spiritual oversight and dependence on God
Church leadership is chosen by popularity without spiritual considerations
Elders are appointed solely for administrative tasks
Spiritual discipline is unnecessary for church growth
questions.correctAnswer: The church ordains elders with prayer and fasting, emphasizing spiritual oversight and dependence on God
questions.explanation: Acts 14:23 describes ordination of elders accompanied by prayer and fasting, highlighting the spiritual and divine aspect in church leadership.

questions.question: What theological significance does the reaction of the people in Acts 14:11-13 have regarding the pagan understanding of divinity?
options: It reveals the tendency to deify human agents and misinterpret divine power
It confirms that all pagan gods were true divine beings
It shows that pagan worship was fully aligned with Christian truth
It indicates that miracles always lead to true faith
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals the tendency to deify human agents and misinterpret divine power
questions.explanation: Acts 14:11-13 shows the crowd calling Paul and Barnabas gods and preparing sacrifice, illustrating pagan idolatry's misattribution of divine power to humans.
